sources.fullCitation: “Song Writers to Perform: Lew Pollack and Sidney Mitchell, authors of song hits, who will be among the featured artists at the President’s Ball. The ball opens at 8:45 tonight at the Valencia Ball Room and the proceeds will be devoted to the fight against infantile paralysis.” Photograph with caption. Santa Ana Journal (Santa Ana, Calif.), vol. 3, no. 231, 27 January 1938, p. 7. California Digital Newspaper Collection, University of California, Riverside. Accessed 26 August 2026.

sources.researchNote: The evening belongs to the birthday balls held across the country for the president and the campaign against infantile paralysis that had just been founded, and the two men appear as working songwriters engaged to perform, not as guests. The caption names Pollack and his partner Sidney Mitchell without saying which is which, and the picture is left unattributed on that point. It is the only likeness of Pollack gathered here, and it stands nine years after the song of his that enters the Kaper record.

media.title: Lew Pollack and Sidney Mitchell before the President’s Ball — Santa Ana Journal, 1938
media.description: Press photograph published in the Santa Ana Journal on 27 January 1938 under the heading “Song Writers to Perform”: Lew Pollack and Sidney Mitchell seated over a sheet of music before appearing at the President’s Ball. The printed caption is reproduced beneath the picture.
media.altText: Two men in suits seated side by side under a table lamp, one holding a sheet of paper, with the newspaper caption printed beneath.
media.rightsNote: Reuse rights are not cleared. No photographer or agency is credited, and a United States issue of 1938 kept its copyright only if the registration was renewed after twenty-eight years; the inventory of first periodical renewals kept at the University of Pennsylvania has no entry for this title, which records no renewal but does not prove that none was made. The digitising library states no rights position of its own. The local 268 × 297 pixel reproduction is used for the identification of the sitters alone, with the newspaper, the holding collection and the unresolved renewal stated alongside it.
